description: From the fz-kdt.130 refutation (2026-09-02, PRE-EXISTING at c2041041e and after): Enum.reduce([1,2,3], 0, f) where f came from receive -- interp 'closure call ... omitted callee value 9 but target 14 needs semantic inputs' (fz-kdt.111's signature family); JIT/AOT error[artifact/incomplete-semantic-plan], AOT fails to BUILD. The natural next shape after 130's fixtures and the one a user hits first. (Enum.map with a mailbox closure WORKS after 130 -- was silently wrong at base.) Suspect: the reducer's callable-demand path meeting the no-summary mailbox callable (130's carrier rule covers direct closure_call edges; the Enum HOF path goes through callable-flow construction instead). Triage against fz-kdt.111/127 machinery.

comments.text:
Fixed in 599728c9b (worktree wt-kdt152-build, based on 62b5b09fe).

MECHANISM (one root, and it is NOT the construction layer the ticket suspected):

Enum.reduce/3 hands its reducer down to List.reduce_cont/3, which specializes on
the ACCUMULATOR: the first step is reached at the literal accumulator's type
(acc: int) and every later step at the reducer's widened return (acc: any). So
one callable input -- reduce_cont's semantic input 2 -- reaches TWO activations
of one lambda (Enum.reduce/3#lambda at [any,int,int] and at [any,int,any]).

exact_direct_callable_layout (jobs/transport.rs) asked how many TARGETS the
position's settled target set names and bailed on 'targets.len() != 1', falling
through to joined_transport_layout. The callable is not first-class (opaque=false,
escape=false -- the OPAQUE thing is one level in, the user reducer it captures),
so the joined layout came back as callable(<unknown>/0 lanes=[]) carrier=Absent:
NOTHING. Meanwhile materialize_closure_call_edge still ground a direct call to
one of the two (fz-kdt.132's rule -- the argument types decide), and that
activation's input 0 is the mailbox callable at carrier=ValueRef, needing a
capture lane that no longer existed. Interp's missing_direct_callee check and
native's direct_closure_capture_lanes both said exactly that.

FIX: a transport layout is pure physics, so the question is how many LAYOUTS,
not how many targets. Several activations of one function describe the same
captures, so they name one layout and the value travels as those captures;
which activation a callsite reaches is decided at the callsite, so that choice
never travels with the value. exact_direct_callable_layout now names one
CallableDescr per target and settles when they agree; disagreement still means
no exact layout and still falls back to the joined layout. The old one-target
case is that same rule with one member.

The mailbox is load-bearing in the witness only because a reducer the compiler
can NAME has no surviving capture lane -- carrying nothing was then accidentally
the right answer.

EVIDENCE: fixtures2/behavior/mailbox_closure_reduce.fz (int acc, list acc,
capturing reducer, empty-list control) red at base on all three doors with this
ticket's exact signature, green after against its Elixir oracle;
mailbox_closure_enum_hofs.fz pins map+filter with mailbox callables (green at
base too -- the neighbours that did NOT break). Unit tripwire
compiler2_transport_plan_carries_captures_when_one_layout_covers_several_activations
is red at base with CallableDescr { function: None, capture_lanes: [] }.

GATES: lib 1574/0/5, cli 24/0, matrix 464/0/9 (+6), aot_variadic_open 1/0,
clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, release clean. Corpus canon sweep (460
dumping fixtures): 7 movers, 366 lines, EVERY line an anonymous
callable(<unknown>/0 ... lanes=[]) becoming its named callable -- lanes=[] and
carrier=Absent on both sides (183/183), zero physical movement. Corpus behaviour
sweep 1176 runs: 0 differences. FIFO/LIFO: same 3 schedule-dependent canon
fixtures at base and head; head-under-LIFO == base-under-FIFO on all 1176 runs.
New fixtures: canon byte-identical over 10 compiles, output identical over 20x
JIT and 20x AOT, 0.34s/0.47s to compile.

Doc: .agent/docs/semantic-fixpoint.md states the layout rule beside fz-kdt.130's
carrier rule.

BYCATCH, both pre-existing and verified identical at base and after:
fz-kdt.155 (P1) Enum.each with a mailbox closure prints one element then aborts
on JIT/AOT (capture-tag mismatch, interp correct) -- the one Enum HOF still red,
which is why it could not be pinned as a companion here; fz-kdt.156
Enum.reduce with a TUPLE accumulator is error[lower/unbound] on every door even
with a static lambda (not mailbox-related at all).

LANDED e132fe768 (2026-09-02; refuter verdict MERGE outright — first unconditional MERGE of the campaign; two doc-precision fixes folded anyway per the provable-fact law: 'disagree about the captures' → full CallableDescr equality incl. function; the Cut/Waiting comment now covers both cases + the BTreeSet-order note). Refuter highlights: agreement = full structural equality = the same equality intern_callable pools on, so a physics false-agree is INEXPRESSIBLE; 127's shape refuses by construction; the multi-target path fires on exactly 9 fixtures corpus-wide with ZERO disagreements; the grounded-direct/fallback triangle is NARROWED not closed (pre-existing, fail-loud, unreachable at head — noted); THE FIX IS BROADER THAN ITS FIXTURES: five more all-doors-red shapes go green (joined mailbox reducers, tuple accumulator via mailbox, int+float accumulators, reducer-capturing-closure, one reducer at two callsites); 2625-run three-door sweep = exactly one difference, the fix. Bycatch verdicts: fz-kdt.155 correctly scoped; fz-kdt.156 MISDIAGNOSED (re-scoped); refusal-half coverage gap → fz-kdt.157.
